title: Audio V9 is the first heterogeneous deployment proof
summary: Audio V9 proves the generic component against a heterogeneous Linux fleet. The deployment package stages one content-addressed release, reuses compatible native/runtime artifacts, rebuilds Foreign Runtime where target loadability fails, verifies the corpus, and deliberately keeps worker start separate.
invariants: Audio-specific corpus meaning and processing semantics remain outside Deployment.
Foreign Runtime ABI mismatch is repaired by host-native rebuild, not loader-path manipulation.
Compatible hosts reuse the packaged runtime; incompatible hosts rebuild from authoritative source.
The same deployment generation can be staged across heterogeneous hosts while readiness results differ by observed target state.
A corpus/hash failure blocks READY even when package staging itself succeeded.

provenance.claim: Defines Audio as first consumer and exact runtime/native readiness behavior.
Shows the same generation staged and an Audio readiness/corpus gate succeeding on a host.
Shows heterogeneous fleet READY/BUILDING results after common staging.
Shows corpus SHA-256 verification failure/timeout blocks readiness on two hosts.
